title: Incident Taxonomy Inconsistency x Pattern Detection: Why Fragmented Reporting Blinds an AI-NTSB

original_idea.body:
# Incident Taxonomy Inconsistency x Pattern Detection: Why Fragmented Reporting Blinds an AI-NTSB

**Problem:** AI incident reports use inconsistent taxonomies; an NTSB-style body needs to aggregate to detect systemic patterns. Inconsistent labels prevent clustering.

**Direction:** Pull AI Incident Database entries, apply 2-3 public AI-harm taxonomies, measure classification divergence, show clustering fragmentation, test a normalization mapping.

**Why it matters:** Demonstrates AI-NTSB value depends on taxonomy harmonization. Open dataset, beginner-friendly clustering.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2501.14778; arXiv:2511.05914; AI Incident Database.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (better incident aggregation aids systemic-risk detection) but catastrophic-risk link is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Public dataset + simple clustering/labeling; guided beginner work.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (divergence measure + normalization test) with few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open dataset, civil-society infrastructure work labs won't own.

novelty.reasoning: Incident-taxonomy standardization is studied; the clustering-fragmentation demonstration may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Taxonomy harmonization is an active topic; the specific fragmentation-clustering demo may be open.
